title: Peachy Parallel Assignments (EduHPC 2025)
problem: Limited availability of high-quality, easy-to-adopt assignments for teaching parallel and distributed computing; instructors need inspiring, tested assignments for course adoption.
motivation: Edu* workshops provide curated, instructor-tested assignments. High-quality assignments inspire students and ease adoption across institutions. Parallel computing education benefits from diverse, problem-motivated assignments.
method: The paper presents three parallel computing assignments that have been tested with students and designed for other instructors to adopt easily. The assignments span different domains: a biological simulation (cellular automata, where cells on a grid evolve by following rules), a physics model of water flowing downhill with rainfall on uneven terrain, and a machine learning operation called softmax (which converts raw numbers into probabilities). Each teaches parallelization by tackling a problem that naturally breaks into independent pieces that can run simultaneously across multiple processors.
key_novelty: The contribution is curating parallel assignments across diverse motivations—biology, physics simulation, and machine learning—so students see parallelization as practical and broadly useful, not just theoretical.
contributions: Fairy rings assignment: biological simulation parallelization
Flooding simulation: environmental modeling with active constraints
Softmax parallel implementation: deep learning motivation
Tested in real courses with demonstrated effectiveness
Design for easy adoption by other instructors
limitations: Complexity levels and target course types not specified
Scalability and performance metrics not discussed
primary_theme: Curated parallel computing assignments for HPC education
